scale: 0 to 10 per observed criterion; weighted total out of 100
scope: A session evaluation, not universal certification of NativePeers

criteria.name: Cross-vendor native collaboration
criteria.full_score: The requested different-vendor native sessions complete useful work with correct observed model, identity, home and effective tools; results reach the intended parent and can be used without manual copying or invented completion.

criteria.name: Isolation, attribution and recoverability
criteria.full_score: Observed work preserves unrelated files, sessions and provider state; source/worker deltas and ownership are clear; failed or interrupted attempts remain recoverable; integration and cleanup use the actual recorded scope.

criteria.name: Delivery and completion lifecycle
criteria.full_score: Admission, native ingestion, model acknowledgment and completion are correctly distinguished; failures and later phases are intelligible; actual quiet close-out preserves the final visible response with genuine delayed frames retained and no extra chat turns.

criteria.name: Agent usability and context efficiency
criteria.full_score: A bounded task uses a compact prepared context, visible compatible tools and separate budget dimensions; ordinary preparation/results need no avoidable manual reconstruction, redundant diagnostic loop, oversized historical payload or permission escalation.

criteria.name: Practical productivity
criteria.full_score: Delegation or coordination produces demonstrated useful findings, integration or parallel progress whose value justifies measured orchestration/intervention costs; task slicing is appropriate and unrelated compilation or the parent agent's mistakes are not charged to the tool.

criteria.name: Novelty, differentiation and workflow fit
criteria.full_score: The session demonstrates a distinct practical native-session benefit over its realistic simpler alternative, using existing capabilities with little friction. Full credit does not require claiming invention of agent messaging or an exhaustive novelty search.

anchors.0: Observed unusable or harmful behavior for the criterion.
anchors.2: Repeated failure; the intended useful outcome was not reached.
anchors.4: Useful capability exists, but material failures or manual recovery dominate.
anchors.6: Useful outcome with substantial friction or incomplete measured benefit.
anchors.8: Reliable observed outcome with minor bounded friction.
anchors.10: The criterion's complete full-score behavior is observed and supported.

rules: Use intermediate numeric scores when supported; keep the weights fixed for comparisons.
Missing observations are null, not zero or ten; report observed weight as coverage.
An overall score is reported only at 100 percent coverage; partial evaluations retain per-criterion scores.
A 100 requires native-result evidence and no unresolved recorded failures; source-only checks are insufficient.
Separate tool defects, agent orchestration mistakes, provider limits and external build costs.
Historical scores remain immutable. Revisions retain the old record and share a session key so aggregates count only the latest revision per session.
Compare complete session scores and per-criterion sample counts; do not call observational scores a controlled benchmark.
